A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ComFe study. The complete main texts and Appendices A-D, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison across the changed layout and numbering.

before.justification: v5 reports original ComFe classification, robustness, efficiency and FunnyBirds results, together with appendix ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and adds a combined auxiliary-loss ablation in Table S10.

M1.justification: The frozen ViT backbone, transformer decoder, image and class prototypes, prediction procedure and specified losses remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. The revised probabilistic justification does not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine classification datasets, four ImageNet generalisation and robustness datasets, and FunnyBirds. The added comparisons and ablation retain existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DINOv2-based comparisons reported by Zhu et al. (2025): ProtoPNet, TesNet, EvalProtoPNet and ProtoNonParam with additional fine-tuned blocks, plus frozen ProtoNonParam. This expands one comparison while retaining the previous comparators.

E3.justification: The added Table 1 comparisons introduce configurations with five additional fine-tuned transformer blocks and a frozen ProtoNonParam configuration. Table S10 adds a control disabling all three auxiliary losses simultaneously. Previously stated ComFe training budgets and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table S10 extends the existing individual-loss removals with joint removal of all three auxiliary losses. Appendix A also newly reports that including the image-prototype marginal hurts performance, without quantitative support. Other ablations, robustness analyses and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both Appendix D introductions specify five runs and reporting mean and standard deviation. The added ablation follows this existing practice, and the seed-specific appendix examples are retained. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds baseline outcomes, including TesNet at 89.0% on CUB and 82.6% on Cars, and frozen ProtoNonParam at 78.0% on CUB. Table S10 adds all-losses-off results of 75.5±1.3, 94.1±0.8 and 90.3±0.5 for Aircraft, Pets and Cars. Existing ComFe scores remain unchanged; the fine-tuned baseline results use different training conditions.

T1.justification: v5 presents exact marginalization and identifies the clustering loss with the negative log marginal likelihood. v6 Section 3 and Appendix A introduce continuous latent-variable integrals and MLE point approximations, then distinguish the marginal likelihood from the chosen clustering loss by dropping the image-prototype marginal. This substantially revises the central probabilistic justification while retaining the specified loss.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the claims of an intrinsically interpretable, scalable classification head with competitive performance, improved robustness and consistent hyperparameters. Added explanations and comparisons do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The new Discussion explicitly addresses unfamiliar inputs for frozen backbones, selecting or ensembling heads, and why classification confidence maps need not cover entire objects. It discusses segmentation supervision or foreground extraction as possible extensions. Seed variability and background-feature reliance were already documented in v5; v6 adds qualifications and possible responses.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies Xavier-normal decoder initialization, spherical-uniform class prototypes, standard-normal queries, 224×224 inputs and bilinear upsampling. These refine previously incomplete documentation rather than establish changed settings. Appendix A replaces the explicit background-association matrix construction with prose; code access remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v6 adds positioning against ProtoNonParam and citations supporting TesNet, EvalProtoPNet, amortized inference and foundation-model limitations. It also expands comparison with ProtoP approaches. The established research positioning largely remains, while numerous publication and bibliographic updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: v6 adds a Discussion section, moves prototype parameterization before likelihood derivation, expands selected explanations and makes local language edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain recognizable. Citation style and author affiliations also change.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to a single-column format with extensively rearranged and resized displays. v6 adds the framework summary diagram as Figure 3, expands Tables 1 and S10, and redistributes appendix figures. Existing empirical image content is retained despite renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: v6 improves transparency by explicitly identifying mathematical approximations, documenting initialization and resolution, and clarifying applicability limits. The additional DINOv2 comparisons and combined-loss ablation strengthen focused parts of the evidence. These gains outweigh the reduced explicitness of the background-matrix construction, but the method and established empirical results remain stable, and fine-tuned baseline comparisons still require qualification.
